data.title: Century Complete Celebrates Model Home Grand Opening at Cates Bay Crossing in Conway, South Carolina
data.description:
New community brings 94 homesites to well-connected location 15 miles from Myrtle Beach

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Grand Opening Details: The Nov. 21 model home Grand Opening at Cates Bay Crossing will feature tours and an appearance from members of Minor League Baseball team, The Myrtle Beach Pelicans.
  • Floor Plans Designed for Real Life: Cates Bay Crossing offers five one- and two-story floor plans priced from the $260s. Select plans feature versatile living spaces such as flex rooms, gamerooms, and private studies.
  • Move-In Ready Options: Cates Bay Crossing features a mix of move-in ready homes and winter move-in homes, for buyers seeking a faster new construction timeline.  
  • Thoughtful Included Features: Every Cates Bay Crossing home includes quartz countertops, LG® stainless-steel appliances, and Kohler® fixtures, providing style and functionality.
  • Compelling Location: Located in the charming town of Conway, Cates Bay Crossing is about 35 minutes from beautiful Myrtle Beach, popular dining and shopping destinations, and waterfront attractions, as well as dozens of world-class golf courses.

CONWAY, S.C., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Century Communities, Inc. ()—a top national homebuilder, industry leader in online home sales, and featured on America's Most Trustworthy Companies by Newsweek—will host a model home Grand Opening at Cates Bay Crossing, a Century Complete community in Conway, South Carolina, offering new homes from the $260s.

The event will take place on Saturday, Nov. 21, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Visitors can tour the new model home and meet members of The Myrtle Beach Pelicans, the local Minor League Baseball team, who will be in attendance from noon to 2 p.m.

Learn more and RSVP for the Grand Opening at www.CenturyCommunities.com/CatesBaySC.

Cates Bay Crossing's location makes it an attractive choice for a new home, with Myrtle Beach about 15 miles from the community—putting natural beauty, outdoor recreational opportunities, and waterfront attractions in easy reach.

Downtown Conway's Riverwalk, shops and dining are nearby, and Pee Dee Elementary School, Whittemore Park Middle School, and Conway High School are each less than eight miles away. Nicknamed the "Golf Capital of the World," Myrtle Beach also features dozens of golf courses for residents to enjoy.

Homebuyers seeking space for growing households will find versatile living spaces—including flex rooms, studies, gamerooms, and lofts—that can be adapted to fit current and future needs.

Designer-selected standard features include quartz countertops, white Shaker-style cabinets, LG® stainless-steel kitchen appliances, luxury vinyl plank flooring, and Kohler® fixtures.

data.title: Copper Lake Announces Grant of Stock Options
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Copper Lake Resources Ltd. (FSE: W0I0) ("Copper Lake" or the "Company") announces that its Board of Directors has granted an aggregate of 4,100,000 incentive stock options (the "Options") to directors, officers and consultants of the Company pursuant to the Company's stock option plan.

Each Option entitles the holder to purchase one common share of the Company at an exercise price of $0.25 per share until November 18, 2031. The Options vested immediately upon grant. Of the Options granted, 1,650,000 were granted to directors and officers of the Company and 2,450,000 were granted to consultants of the Company.

The Options, and any common shares issued upon the exercise of the Options prior to March 19, 2027, are subject to a four-month hold period in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange. The grant of the Options is subject to the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

ABOUT COPPER LAKE RESOURCES

Copper Lake Resources Ltd. is a publicly traded Canadian mineral exploration and development company with interests in two projects both located in Ontario.

The Marshall Lake high-grade VMS copper, zinc, silver and gold project, comprises an area of approximately 220 square km located 120 km north of Geraldton, Ontario and is just 22 km north of the main CNR rail line. Copper Lake has an 82.97% interest in the joint ventured property, which consists of 233 claims and 52 mining leases. The project also includes 148 claim cells staked in 2018 and 2020 that are 100% owned and not subject to any royalties. These newer claims add approximately 30 square km to the property.

In addition to the original Marshall Lake property above, Marshall Lake also includes the Sollas Lake and Summit Lake properties, which are 100% owned by the Company and are not subject to any royalties. The Sollas Lake property consists of 20 claim cells comprising an area of 4 square km on the east side of the Marshall Lake property where historical EM airborne geophysical surveys have outlined strong conductors on the property hosted within the same favorable felsic volcanic units. The Summit Lake property currently consists of 100 claim cells comprising an area of 20.5 square km, is accessible year-round, and is located immediately west of the original Marshall Lake property. The Marshall Lake project is located in the traditional territories of Aroland and Animbiigoo Zaagi'igan Anishinaabek ("AZA") First Nations.

Copper Lake has a 69.79% joint venture interest in the Norton Lake nickel, copper, cobalt, and palladium PGM property, located in the southern Ring of Fire area, is approximately 100 km north of the Marshall Lake Property. The Company filed an updated NI 43-101 in October 2023 with a mineral resource of open pit and underground Measured + Indicated Resources of 1,795,000 tonnes at an average grade of 0.72% NI, 0.69% Cu, 339 ppm Co, 0.52 g/t Pd, 0.17 g/t Pt and containing 28.3Mlbs of nickel and 27.3Mlbs of copper. The Norton Lake property is located in the traditional territories of Eabametoong ("Fort Hope") and Neskantaga First Nations.

data.title: Wall Street Giants Shift From Tech Bets to Balanced Hedging in Third-Quarter 13F Filings
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Shanghai Securities News, third-quarter 13F filings showed major investment firms cutting positions in broad U.S. stock ETFs and reallocating within technology and toward defensive sectors. Bridgewater reduced its holdings in the SPDR S&P 500 ETF and iShares Core S&P 500 ETF by 36% and 50%, respectively, while Renaissance Technologies sold all 219,000 of its SPDR S&P 500 ETF shares. Millennium Management cut its position in that fund from 4.857 million shares to 2.4 million. Barclays reduced its SPDR S&P 500 ETF holdings by 11% and its Nasdaq-100 ETF holdings by 47%; JPMorgan cut its Nasdaq-100 ETF position by 22%.

Renaissance Technologies sharply reduced its holdings in Nvidia, Apple, Amazon and Meta, while increasing its Micron position from 210,000 shares to 1.52 million, AMD from 830,000 to 2 million, and Sandisk from 4,980 to 276,500. Bridgewater also cut its Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft holdings, while more than doubling its Micron position and increasing its Sandisk stake from 317 shares to 66,800.

Fidelity International increased holdings in AstraZeneca, Agnico Eagle Mines and Bank of Nova Scotia. UBS opened a position of 13.81 million shares in Exxon Mobil and added 610,000 Chevron shares. BlackRock, Vanguard Capital Management and State Street Group also increased their Coca-Cola holdings. As of November 17, AstraZeneca and Coca-Cola had each gained more than 10% since October. Barclays upgraded U.S. health care to “positive” from “neutral” on November 16, citing favorable demand and rising earnings expectations. Standard Chartered recommended diversification across technology, financials, health care and high-dividend stocks in an early-November strategy view.

data.title: Anthropic surpasses SpaceX to become world's biggest IPO, raises $81.3 billion in upsized offering
data.description:
Artificial Intelligence lab Anthropic PBC has raised $81.3 billion in an upsized Initial Public Offering (IPO), making it the biggest in the world, surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX, which debuted only a few months prior.

In an official release on Thursday, November 19, Anthropic stated that it had upsized the offering, selling 980 million shares, instead of the 825 million planned earlier. The company also priced the IPO at $83 apiece, well above the initial range of $70 to $78 per share.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk's SpaceX had raised $75 billion through its IPO and a total of $85.7 billion, after underwriters exercised their overallotment.

Anthropic's release stated that the underwriters have been given a 30-day option to purchase another 147 million shares. Shares will list on the Nasdaq later this evening.

The company's overall market capitalization will depend on the number of shares outstanding, but the price has already put the valuation past the $1.4 trillion that the company had targeted earlier.

While Anthropic has already raised over $81 billion through its IPO, a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and AMD, have collectively agreed to invest $26 billion in the company at the IPO price, which will take the total fund raise past $100 billion. Anthropic is a buyer of costly systems from all of these companies.

Anthropic was co-founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei and a group of researchers who had collectively defected from OpenAI, and has now become a competitive force against Sam Altman's company after developing a family of AI models known as Claude.

As per the latest IPO document, each co-founder is selling 3.38 million shares in the Anthropic IPO, for total proceeds of $1.96 billion.

For the nine months that ended on September 30, Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up nearly 1,200% from the same period last year. The company reported a net loss of $104 billion for the same period, although most of that was due to change in the fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. For the same nine months in 2025, Anthropic had lost $25.1 billion.

An amended filing also disclosed that its revenue run-rate at the end of October was nearly $81 billion, $10 billion higher than the previous month.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus had over 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of the IPO, which included two high-profile disputes with the Trump Administration earlier this year.

“Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles,” Anthropic’s co-founders wrote in the company’s prospectus. “Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort.”

(With Inputs From Agencies)

data.title: Tesla Wins Manitoba Court Order On EV Rebate Ban As Canadian PM Carney Notes Brand’s Fading Cachet
data.description:
Key points:
  • Canadian PM Mark Carney emphasized on Wednesday that Chinese automakers now present the fiercest competition, offering fully electric models packed with advanced AI and high-tech features.
  • Carney also urged the U.S. to act as a more willing partner to Canada and Mexico in the auto sector rather than prolonging a trade war.
  • Last week, a Manitoba court issued an order opening the Canadian province’s decision to block EV rebates for Teslas for cross-examination, Bloomberg reported. 

EV giant Tesla has reportedly obtained a procedural win in its legal challenge to the Canadian province of Manitoba’s decision to bar its vehicles from its electric vehicle rebate program, a dispute rooted in Canada’s broader response to U.S. trade tensions.

Tesla once dominated Canada’s EV market, as noted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney at the DealBook Summit earlier on Wednesday. The company continues to sell in the country but has lost significant market share since. Tesla’s Canadian registrations fell more than 60% in 2025, from roughly 55,000 units in 2024 to an estimated 18,300–20,000.

Manitoba Court Requires Decision Record

Manitoba’s program offers rebates of up to C$4,000 ($2,791) on qualifying EVs. In March 2025, amid escalating U.S.-Canada tariff disputes under President Donald Trump, the province excluded Tesla vehicles as well as those manufactured in China from the rebate program. The exclusion was later extended for another year.

A Manitoba court last week ordered the provincial government to produce a complete record of its decision, supported by an affidavit from a knowledgeable official, within 10 days, opening the door to cross-examination, Bloomberg reported.

Tesla’s Past Dominance And Chinese Competition

Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Carney addressed Canada’s January decision to admit 49,000 Chinese EVs annually at a 6.1% tariff rate, with a firm cap above that volume. He noted that Tesla benefited from the change by shipping vehicles from its Shanghai factory, while it previously shipped vehicles to Canada from its U.S. facilities.

Before 2024, Carney observed, EVs in Canada “were all Teslas.” He acknowledged owning one himself but said he no longer does, adding that resale values have disappointed because the brand no longer holds the same cachet.

“I don’t have it any more, sorry Elon. And I didn’t get the resale value for it that I thought I would because they don’t quite have the cachet that they used to,” Carney said.

Carney emphasized that Chinese automakers now present the fiercest competition, offering fully electric models packed with advanced AI and high-tech features. He argued that North America lags China, as does Europe, and urged the U.S. to act as a more willing partner to Canada and Mexico in the auto sector rather than prolonging a trade war. Trump has signaled plans to raise tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, and parts to 50% starting January 1, 2027.

Tesla’s key global rival, BYD, is currently seeking to compete with the American EV maker in Canada, as are others including Geely and Chery.

How Did TSLA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock stayed within ‘bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'low' levels.

TSLA stock has dropped 15% year-to-date.

data.title: Litchfield Minerals Narrows Harts Range Copper-Nickel Search to Four Priority Areas
data.description:
Litchfield Minerals has narrowed its search for copper and nickel at Harts Range in the Northern Territory to four priority areas after completing a major geophysical survey.

The work examined about 1,100 square kilometres, identifying potential exploration sites around a much deeper feature that may help explain how metals moved through the region.

Completed by Vox Geophysics under the 2026 BHP Xplor program, the surveys combined measurements of underground electrical conductivity and rock density to identify places worthy of closer examination.

Litchfield has sent a field team to inspect the four areas, although the results do not yet demonstrate that any contains copper or nickel mineralisation.

More Focused Copper Search

The company is investigating two ways copper deposits can form, both involving metals travelling through the ground before accumulating in favourable rocks.

In one, metal-bearing magma rises from deep underground and can form copper-nickel sulphides where it encounters sulphur-bearing rocks.

In the other, hot fluids move through faults and fractures, depositing copper in rock layers where conditions allow it to become concentrated.

The surveys have identified structures that could have provided those routes, giving Litchfield a more focused starting point than the wider geological belt.

The four areas sit where possible metal pathways meet rocks that could have helped concentrate mineralisation, rather than being evidence of discoveries in their own right.

Four Areas Offer Different Clues

Two of the priority areas, IA1 and IA2, follow the boundary between the Irindina and Aileron geological provinces, where faults may have channelled magma or mineral-bearing fluids.

The other two, MT4 and MT6, lie in rock formations associated with unusually strong gravity readings, a combination Litchfield considers worth investigating.

MT6 is within the Riddock Amphibolite, the same rock formation associated with the Basil copper-cobalt deposit, which Litchfield does not own.

The survey also identified a large deep conductor, MT5, from about 3 km to more than 5km underground, beneath a prominent gravity feature and along a projected major fault.

MT5 is too deep to drill directly, but its apparent relationship with some shallower features could help guide exploration closer to the surface.

Field Work to Test Theory

The company is now looking for visible geological evidence over the four priority areas before deciding where to concentrate further spending.

“We are clear that conductors have other possible explanations, and that only field work, further surveys and modelling, and ultimately drilling will tell us what is there,” managing director Matthew Pustahya said.

“That is why our team heads to site this week, while we model the gravity in 3D with the MT to test whether MT5 is dense—the aim is to turn the best of these conductors into drill targets and put our next dollars where the evidence is strongest.”

Planned modelling will examine whether the deep feature contains unusually dense rock, while closer-spaced surveys may help narrow the most promising areas into specific drilling targets.

Litchfield could eventually use the same approach elsewhere across the eastern Irindina region, depending on results, land access, tenure, and funding.

data.title: Weight-loss drugs' hit to UK grocery spending tops £1 billion, Worldpanel says
data.description:
The impact of weight-loss drugs on UK grocery spending has surpassed £1 billion ($1.32 billion), as new pill formats and rising uptake among men accelerate their use, researcher Worldpanel by Numerator said on Thursday.

  • UK households with at least one GLP‑1 user spent more than £1 billion less on groceries than expected in the year after adoption compared with households without a GLP-1 user, Worldpanel said

  • The proportion of British households with a user of GLP-1 drugs, such as Eli Lilly's Mounjaro or Novo Nordisk's Wegovy, has risen from 6.3% in February this year to 8.5% in August

  • Growth is accelerating. In the six-month period, user numbers of GLP-1 injections and pills rose almost as much as they did in the whole of the previous year

  • Despite regulatory approval only coming in June, pills, account for 11.2% of UK GLP-1 users

  • Men are also driving growth, making up 32% of users, up from 23% in February

  • Worldpanel by Numerator is a global consumer data company. Its survey data of what British households buy drew from a total sample of 9,629

  • The £1 billion figure of displaced spending from Britain's grocery market is equivalent to £389 a year displaced from each user households' shopping baskets.

  • Spending on alcohol and crisps among users has fallen 15% more than in non-user households

  • In contrast, easy, portion-controlled options are gaining ground. Volume sales of frozen ready meals have risen 30% among users

  • Worldpanel said its estimates suggested that GLP-1 usage was set to surpass 10% of British households in 2027

($1 = 0.7578 pounds)

data.title: UK finance sector cyber incidents hit second-highest level in five years
data.description:
By Phoebe Seers

Cyber incidents reported to Britain's financial watchdog in October hit their second-highest monthly level in five years, underscoring the growing threat facing the financial sector.

The Financial Conduct Authority said the number of incidents reported in October was more than 50% higher than the previous peak recorded 18 months earlier.

The FCA, together with the Bank of England, also proposed new guidance aimed at giving banks, insurers and other financial firms clearer expectations on how to prepare for, detect and recover from cyberattacks.

Earlier this month, French lender Credit Mutuel Arkéa said hackers had stolen around €100 million ($113 million) in a cyber heist, while crypto exchange Binance said hackers had drained $6.3 billion of digital assets.

Katharine Braddick, chief executive of Britain's Prudential Regulation Authority and deputy governor at the Bank of England, said cyberattacks were becoming more frequent, complex and damaging.

"Regulators need confidence both that firms have strong cyber controls and that they can detect, contain and recover quickly from incidents," she said.

The total of 38 incidents reported to the FCA in October was the second highest in five years, surpassed only by the 49 reported in June 2023 during the .

The proposed guidance sets out more detailed expectations on cyber resilience, governance, incident response, recovery and supply-chain risks. It builds on existing operational resilience requirements rather than introducing new regulatory obligations.

A consultation closes on February 26.

The regulators also issued additional guidance on managing cyber risks linked to frontier AI and future advances in quantum computing.

data.title: Globetrotting with Purpose, Planning with AI: Agoda Reveals How South Koreans Plan to Travel in 2027
data.description:
SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Digital travel platform Agoda has published its 2027 Asia Travel Pulse, spotlighting five key trends and insights poised to shape the next year of travel in Asia and South Korea. Agoda's report points to increased appetite for international travel, alongside the rapid rise of AI in trip planning and growing interest in experiences that reflect travelers' passions, from food and culture to shopping and outdoor pursuits.

Based on research across more than 3,300 travelers from 11 markets in Asia, the 2027 Agoda Asia Travel Pulse also reveals that South Korean travelers are making considered choices about how they spend. Many expect to take fewer but longer trips, while looking for strong value and greater ease across the whole journey.

Alex Park, Country Director, South Korea at Agoda, said: "South Korean travelers have always been curious about the world, and in 2027 that curiosity is stronger than ever. More than half now plan to travel mostly internationally and they know exactly what they're going for: rich culture and, of course, great food. It's also exciting to see that they're among Asia's most AI-savvy travelers. Agoda will continue to make it easier for South Korean travelers to plan and book trips that are personal, seamless, and great value."

Agoda's top five trends defining travel in South Korea in 2027:

  • International travel interest remains a priority, despite cost considerationsFollowing a year of strong interest in overseas travel, South Koreans are looking to travel abroad even more next year. More than a half (51%) of respondents expect to travel mostly outside their own country in 2027—compared with 39% last year—making international travel the leading plan. South Korea ranked third among the 11 markets surveyed for international travel appetite, 13 percentage points above the regional average of 38%. Cost remains a key consideration: more than a third (36%) of respondents say lower travel costs would most help them travel more.
  • AI becomes a trusted travel planner, with travelers in controlSouth Korean travelers are increasingly turning to AI to plan their trips, with 60% now using it for travel planning, up from 36% last year. This places South Korea third among AI adoption for the 11 markets surveyed. Still, travelers want to stay in control of their bookings: 39% would only allow an AI agent to book a hotel on their behalf if they could review the booking before confirming, while 34% prefer to book hotels themselves. In 2027, trust will shape the way forward for AI: South Korean travelers say real reviews, clear sources of information and explanations behind recommendations would increase their confidence.
  • Cuisine and culture top the travel menuCulinary experiences are the leading motivation for South Koreans planning to travel in 2027, followed by cultural exploration and shopping. Notably, South Korea stands out for its interest in cultural experiences, with 69% of respondents citing cultural exploration as a travel motivation, 15 percentage points above the regional average.Personal interests and hobbies are also a key driver of travel choices, with 69% of respondents saying these influence their decisions. Meanwhile, social media and environmental considerations are gaining prominence, cited by 31% and 34% of South Korean respondents, respectively, up from 13% and 4% last year.
  • Making each trip count: interest in fewer trips, longer stays South Korean travelers are trading trip frequency for value. The most common plan for next year is to take one to three trips (53%), up from 30% last year. At the same time, the number of travelers expecting their trips to last thirteen days or longer has tripled compared with last year. For many, the goal is no longer to travel more often, but to travel better, go further, and stay longer.
  • Destination comes first, while location matters most in accommodation choicesFour in five South Korean travelers (80%) say choosing a destination is their first step when planning a leisure trip, the highest share among the 11 markets surveyed and 16 percentage points above the regional average. Accommodation comes next, with location emerging as the top consideration for 39% of respondents, followed by reviews and ratings (25%). Only 18% cite price as their top consideration when choosing accommodation, the lowest share in Asia and 14 percentage points below the regional average of 32%, indicating that South Koreans are more likely to seek out convenience and comfort over value.

Those making travel plans for 2027 can enjoy Agoda's offerings of over 6 million holiday properties, more than 130,000 flight routes, and over 300,000 activities, all easily combined in a single booking. Discover the best deals on Agoda's mobile app and visit Agoda.com for more information.

SOURCE Agoda

data.title: Gold Catches Breath But Stays at Over One-Year Lows — Market Talk
data.description: Gold gains 0.4% early in Asian trade but remains at more than one-year lows as markets price in rate increases from the Fed. The precious metal has been under pressure from a strong dollar and expectations that the Fed will tilt more hawkish to rein in inflation. Minutes from the Fed's October meeting cemented those views, showing that nearly all members thought tighter policy will ultimately be needed under their most likely scenario for the economy. A few warned that inflation might prove stickier than expected, which could necessitate a shift to a more restrictive stance. Chart-wise, it's difficult to spot any significant level of support until prices hit $3,500 an ounce, says David Morrison at Trade Nation. Gold last at $3,739 an ounce. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
